utterances.text: I will complete your testimony. We would like to thank you very much, but I have one question I would like to ask, a personal question, if you do not want to answer, do not. How do you live now? Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They have killed my son, they have killed my soul, they have broken up my family, may God punish them and it is up to the court to judge them. I am now living in Zenica, this is the fifth year, with five women members of the family. We are somehow living, one of my daughters got married, I have another one with me, the two of us are living together. My daughter-in-law has left with my granddaughter. That is how it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Tribunal thanks you very sincerely, and praises you for your courage and wishes you a future filled with serenity and peace. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, can we have the witness escorted out of the courtroom. We will now break until 4.45. The hearing is suspended. (The witness withdrew) (4.15 pm) (A short break) (4.45 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Please have the accused brought in, please. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is Witness H?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness H, you are going to be shown your identity on a piece of paper, but we ask you not to say it out loud, it is just so the Tribunal can be sure that you are the person whose name is on the piece of paper. We will allow you to remain seated to read your declaration. The usher is going to give you a piece of paper on which you have in your own language the oath that you will be asked to take. We will listen to you. WITNESS H (sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The English booth cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness H, you have agreed -- there is a technical problem for the English booth who are not hearing the witness very clearly. Perhaps the microphones were not on? The English booth did not hear. Are the microphones on now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness speak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, do you hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is it coming through for you, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I am going to ask you to repeat the oath, it is just for a technical reason, I hope this does not disturb you to re-read it, to hear your voice and be sure the English booth can hear you. WITNESS H (resworn)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Only static is coming through here. We cannot hear the judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You were called as a witness by the Prosecution, and you will be asked a certain number of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can hear now. May we test --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You will be asked questions by the Prosecutor, after which the Prosecutor is finished. Once he is finished the Defence attorneys will ask you questions. Please relax, you are under the protection of the Tribunal. Protective measures were taken for you to guarantee that your safety is absolute. Mr. Kehoe, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, your Honours. Good afternoon, Witness H.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H, you moved to Ahmici in November 1992 from the Travnik area, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You lived in the village of Ahmici from November 1992 until the events of 16th April 1993, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, Witness H, you are Muslim, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you moved to Ahmici in November 1992, did you move with your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Without giving the names of those individuals right now, who did you move with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came with my husband and three sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we begin, Witness H, you and I have looked at a photograph, an aerial photograph of the village of Ahmici, have we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You have assisted me in pointing out various locations that are important for your testimony, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, to move things along, what I propose, without putting the map on the ELMO, because it would identify where the Witness H lives, if we could give this aerial, one to the witness, to the Defence and obviously the judges, we could follow along and she would be permitted to tell her story without putting this on the ELMO, and we will not have to go into closed session. Mr. President and your Honours, this is an enlargement, as it says, of Exhibit 50 and I believe for the record, Mr. Registrar, it is Exhibit 123.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think this is 125.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, 125. Witness H, this is the map that is before you, that is what we have been working on, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On this particular map, which number corresponds to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the house marked as 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H, let me take you to the morning of 16th April 1993. Can you tell the judges in your own words what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The day of 16th April came, that day was Friday. We were asleep and we were awakened by two bursts of fire. My husband and I got up, looked through the window and saw that the houses in the direction of the mosque were burning. Then we went and woke up our children and went to the basement. We spent some time in the basement and we heard noises around the house, the house was surrounded, and banging on the door, and they also were -- they also shot the lock through as my husband was going up to open it, then they burst in. My children and I stayed in the house and my husband went out, he then returned in and told us to come out. We went out, but I was very frightened, so I barely made it outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, Witness H. When you were walking up the stairs from the basement, did you hear the soldiers talking to your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the conversation of my husband, he said that he was disabled, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was he a fighter or what did he do in the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not a fighter. He worked as a shoe repairer for the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H, why did your husband work as a shoe repair man and not act as a fighter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was ill, he was not fit to be a fighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What type of sickness did he have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had an ulcer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You and your sons went up from the basement, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted). They were pointing rifles at my husband and my son, and I mean soldiers do that, and they addressed me rudely and they told me to go and take my children with me, but I saw what was coming. Subconsciously I thought, "we have done nothing, they will just take us prisoners", but that did not happen. I hesitated, but I did not dare look at them, I looked down in front of me and they yelled at me to go and take my two children, because they would kill us all, and my younger son pulled me by my clothes and said, "let us go mum, so at least you stay alive". Then I started with my children and they stayed there behind. I think I did not go more than 30 yards and I heard shots, I turned around, my son and my husband were falling down the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would you like to take a break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How many soldiers did you see around your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 15 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just that their faces were painted, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After you saw your husband and your son shot, where did you go on the map, what did you do? If you can just assist the court and show us on the map where you went from point 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, this is not coming through. I cannot hear the judge. I do not hear the judge. Try again, perhaps this headset will work better. Yes, this is better. The interpreter hears now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I had a suggestion to make, Mr. Kehoe. Perhaps for Witness H, she might tell her story spontaneously, as she chooses. I, of course, understand that you have questions that you want to ask, but perhaps you could ask her to specify things she would say. What would you prefer to do? Witness H, would you prefer to tell your story or answer the questions that the Prosecutor is asking? Would you rather speak spontaneously or ask specific questions? He must ask you questions. What would you prefer to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever you think is best, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Continue, Mr. Kehoe, and try simply to distribute your questions as you think fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can just allow the witness to tell her story and just break in when I feel some particular issue needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H, continue to tell the judges what happened after you saw your husband and your son shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted). I was crying, we went on, the houses I could see were burning. We got to a curve in the road, the house of Esad Ahmic was there, Esad Ahmic was lying motionless next to his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is Esad Ahmic's house on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What number is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was Esad Ahmic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately how old was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was about 60. I did not know the man very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue on, Witness H.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I went on with my children, and got to Sulejman Ahmic's house. I did not know whether there was anyone inside, but the house had not been burnt down. We went in, actually we went to the door, tried to open the door, it was not locked, it was opened, and we found there two local ladies, one was called Smaila and the other Raza. The Kulas family were there, Kermo Kulas, brother Dzevad, son Enes, their wives, Kermo's wife Nisveta and Dzevad's wife, Diba. Then there was their daughter, Kermo's daughter, whose name was Enesa, and Kermo's sister Samija, who was retarded. She looked like a child, she did not develop properly. When we entered, I saw Kermo and his brother and his son, Enes, and I told them to flee because my son and husband had been killed. I realised that they were killing the able-bodied men, and he answered, Kermo said, "I do not know where to hide". I said, "you must find somewhere, because they are sure to come here too, because the house has not yet been set on fire". I did not see them again. I was in shock, I did not know what to do, I kept looking at the house where I had lived. I just wanted to go and see my son and husband, to see whether they were still alive. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted). They could not believe him and she asked me, "tell me that this is not true", and I said, "it is true, my son has been killed and my husband". She started screaming aloud. At that moment, I could not even cry. I said, "there are a lot of people here, there are women and children. The lady is gone to sleep, she is afraid, she did not know what to do". I told my sister to look for help and that was the end of the conversation. We stayed on, we knew the soldiers would come again, and they appeared, they broke in roughly and one of the women said, "it is not locked". They were shouting, "open or else we will throw a grenade in", so they opened and they asked whether there were any menfolk. One of these ladies, I do not remember which one, said, "no, there are only women and children here". They told us to get up and to get out as quickly as possible, which we did. We reached the road. Two soldiers were there, and they said, "go on". We started talking to them, asking in which direction we should go and they said, "go wherever you will", and so we took the road which would have led us, I think, to the mosque in Ahmici. There were four soldiers in all in front of the house, and then they separated, two of them went one way and the other two another way. Then these other two who were going towards the mosque, that is the same direction as we, and then they said to us, "where are you going? Go back". They said, "they will use you like human shields if the balijas start shooting at us, then we would get killed", they said. So we went with them, we reached the field between two woods, this was a long and narrow field linking -- linked to the main road. We sat down, we started talking. They were laughing, they were saying, discussing what they should do, whether they should kill us or release us. Then one of them took a rocket launcher and pointed it at the mosque minaret, but they did not fire it. Then he put it down again. We were there, one of them was carrying a big knife, with an orange handle, and he was throwing it a tree, tree trunk, and they were laughing and discussing whether they should let us go or whether they should kill us. We kept quiet, and then this gentleman whom I did not know personally, but Kermo's wife, Nisveta, they came to Sulejman's house before that in Nadioci, his nickname was Rutko, and he said, "what a pretty girl", and that was Nisveta's daughter. She got up but she was holding on to her retarded aunt. Then he asked, "what is happening?", and then at one point she would clap her hands and then again she would start crying. She behaved like a child. They asked, "what is wrong with her, what is wrong with Samija?". Then this lady Nisveta said, "you can see God made her like this, she was born like this". Enesa was standing for a while and then she sat down. They did not do anything to her. Then this lady Smaila, she must have recognised him, he must have been a local boy, because she addressed him and said, "you yellow one", because he had blond hair, "where is my son?", she asked, because she is on Ahmici. Then he said, "he is in God's garden picking flowers", to let her know that her Ivica had been killed. She fell silent. They went on talking and discussing what they should do with us, these two older women, Razija, they addressed them as sons, "look, you have weapons", "you can do what you will, you have killed our men. Let us go, the women and children". He grinned and then he started walking up and down. I was terrified, I was afraid he may go and get drunk and then who knows what they could do to us. I was afraid for my children, he might do something awful. While Rutko and Zuti went off, the situation was different. The soldiers, there was quite a large formation in the woods, they started talking amongst themselves and said, "why do we not let them go?", and then they told us to go. We got up and formed a line one by one. I put my two children in front of me because I did not believe that they had let us go. I thought -- I expected that they might shoot at us at any moment. That did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H, let me stop you there for a second. You were talking before about the soldiers taking you out of Sulejman Ahmic's house. Where is that on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is Sulejman Ahmic's house on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is, it is number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that some soldiers took you to act as human shields. Who told you that you were going to be used as human shields?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two soldiers that I did not know. I had not seen them before. There was Rutko and Zuti. I had mentioned four soldiers, so two were Rutko and Zuti.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was Rutko the one that told you that you were going to be used as a human shield, you and the other women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where were you taken to be used as a human shield? Is it designated here on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You also stated that there were a lot of soldiers spread around that area, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In my discussions with you, you stated that they would have been spread over the area of that line right above the number 4, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, along this whole -- along the line alongside the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know how many soldiers were spread along that line on the woods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you, but there were many. All I know is there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When these soldiers told you that you were going to be used as a human shield, did you see any Armija, Bosnian army soldiers shooting back at them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see any at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that you left the point 4 and you walked in a straight line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where did you walk to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We started walking and got to the house number 1, the house I was living in where my husband and son were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you walked past your house, what condition was your house in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house was burning, and it was caving in, the wooden structure was caving in. It was burning entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you continue to walk past the house to the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in front of house number 1 there was a little amount of space, so we sort of crouched down, we sat down, and we sat there. I got up to peep out to see whether I could see my son and husband, but the children would not let me, nor would the other women. I tried several times. We did not spend much time there. A formation that was going near number 5, a large formation, with black uniforms, they were also going in a group across the road to link up in the area number 4 with this formation that was in the wood. They were talking aloud, "shall we chase them away or kill them?". We crouched down, we did not dare look, we just waited for them to shoot us, but it did not happen. They went past, the formation went by and linked up with this other formation here at number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So Witness H, the soldiers depicted at number 5 walked across the road and linked up with the soldiers that are on the line at number 4, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How many soldiers in black uniforms did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I cannot tell you the figure. There were indeed a lot of them. I really cannot tell you, because I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What happened after that, Witness H?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were sitting there, my sister had asked for help and she probably went to UNPROFOR, there were some that were captured at number 4, and we heard the personnel carriers coming and going, coming to pick up the wounded and we waited for UNPROFOR to come and for us to stop them and that is what happened, so we stopped them right there, near house number 1. We were there in the bend on the road. We told them what had happened, we managed to make them understand, then they showed us with their finger that they would come back and for us to wait. They went off, and since Travnik is quite a long way away, they had to take the wounded and come back and we did not dare wait any longer, because we did not know what fate would befall us, so we agreed to start along the road and let happen what will. So that is what we did, we came to this clearing near house number 1 where I had lived, but I wanted to turn around, and I did and I looked. My son and husband were lying across the stairs. They really were killed, I thought to myself. My children saw this. Then we went on from there and I heard a voice of Ms. Sena Residovic, she was calling out -- Sena Imsirovic, and she called out and we all went together to the place where they were standing, there was Fikreta, the mother-in-law of Imsirovic, and I told her what had happened, "Fikreta, they have killed my son Samir and my husband", and she just said, "they have killed my Galip too, he was her only son". I really fell silent because I realised that I was not the only one to suffer such a tragedy. We started talking, we told them that UNPROFOR had come by and that they had promised to come back for us, so we stayed there for a while. Sena was with her children, her son Emir and daughter Dzenana. Then there was Fahida, her daughter-in-law and her son Enver, also an only son. We spent some time there, then we heard the carriers, the UNPROFOR coming and we ran to meet them. We stopped them, we would not let them go past. They turned around, there were two carriers, they turned around and that is how we got in and then we really started crying, all of us, women. That is my story.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness H -- excuse me. Do you want to take a break, are you okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not want a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is 5.30, you know that there is no hearing -- do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There is no hearing on Monday, so we will resume on Tuesday. Would it be possible to know whether you have many questions you still want to ask, or whether the Defence has many questions to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I just have a couple more questions, Mr. President, and then I am finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do the Defence intend to ask many questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The examination is not completed, of course, but we think this witness can be finished quite soon and would encourage that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: At the suggestion of my colleagues and after having heard what you said, we will try to finish the testimony of Witness H, which would allow you to have the weekend. Since there is no hearing on Monday, perhaps we can just try to go quickly and get to the end. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I just say this, I am very grateful to you for your understanding. May I say that? You are doing your best to finish this because I would like to go back home because of my son, because of his school, and I do appreciate you very much and am very grateful:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Witness H, you said during your testimony that you met Sena and Fikreta and their families. Would you have met them by the house marked on the map as 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, house number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: House number 6 is a house that is owned by a Croat, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that house locked up and vacant on that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house was locked up, even the pigsty. It was also locked. The stable, but in front of the stable there was a kind of cover and there was a pile of firewood underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the map also there is point 7. Is that the point where you were picked up by UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, one last exhibit and if we could just go briefly to private session --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last exhibit, because we are going to identify several names, so if we could go to private session and again not show these photographs on the ELMO, I will be completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that the Defence is nodding its agreement. All right, we will go into private session. (In private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Witness H, good evening, my name is Anto Nobilo, my colleague, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 16th, when this truly terrible tragedy occurred, did you see this man over there? Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did anyone mention him by name on that day in any context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Once again, I turn to Mr. Kehoe, have you any additional questions you would like to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There are no other questions. Turning to my colleagues, Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness H. I am sorry to call you Witness H and not to call you by your name. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my son was a minor, he was under age, and my husband also was never a fighter. I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You told us that there is -- a soldier told that you may be used as human shields. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you hear of anybody who was used as a human shield? Did it happen that some people you know were used as human shields?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of it. I just told you what I had experienced. You have heard my tale and my statement. What I have said really happened and I know nothing more than that, I do not know anything else, because I could not see anything more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Witness H, just one or two questions. You said you saw some soldiers in black uniforms, and that they were going to link up with another group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were wearing black uniforms and they linked up with this formation where we were captured at position 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you able to tell to what group the soldiers in black uniform belonged? Did you see any insignia on their shoulders, or could you tell from their appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see anything, nor did I ever say that I did. I was in a state of shock.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Could you tell the court what kind of uniform the first group of soldiers had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, no, I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But was it or was it not black? I am talking about the first group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what kind of uniform they had, but the second group were in black uniforms, the formation crossing the road at position number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me put it this way to you then. Was the first group of soldiers in the same kind of uniform as the second group of soldiers, or did they have a different kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I must repeat that I cannot remember, I do not know, I cannot remember what kind of uniforms the first group of soldiers had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I accept your answer and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness H, we are finished. You were very courageous and the Tribunal thanks you very sincerely for your testimony. Do you have anything you would like to add, anything you might not have said or anything that you might have liked to have said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what I could say. Let justice win. All that is left for me is to mourn my son for as long as I live and I thank God again for leaving the other two boys with me, so I have some consolation. Let God reward those who do well and punish those who do ill. I ask no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. We can now conclude today's hearing, the Tribunal will withdraw and the usher will help Witness H to return to the witness room and then we wish her godspeed back home. We will resume at 10.00 on Tuesday. (The witness withdrew) (5.50 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
